refresh_token.description: Opaque single-use bearer credential; never an access JWT. Mobile transport (#460 SEC-4A): the Web refresh credential only travels as the HttpOnly granete_web_refresh cookie and is never accepted in a JSON body.

200.description: Rotated access credential; rotated refresh credential via body (mobile) or Set-Cookie (web)

Set-Cookie.description: Web transport only: granete_web_refresh=<opaque>; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/api/auth; Secure (production); expires at the session's absolute bound. Never present for mobile/sketchup transports.

session_id.description: Server-side session registry id (#460). Present on tokens of version 5+; absent while a pre-#460 token is exchanged. Becomes required when the #460 SEC-9 gate retires version 4.

refresh_token.description: Opaque single-use refresh credential. Mobile-only transport (#460 SEC-4A): the mobile client stores it in its secure-store flow. Web never receives a refresh secret in JSON — its rotating credential is delivered exclusively as the HttpOnly granete_web_refresh Set-Cookie.

refresh_expires_at.description: Never later than the auth session absolute expiry. Mobile transport only.

access_expires_at.description: Server-clock instant the returned access token expires (#460 SEC-4A). Mirrors the minting arithmetic exactly so clients can schedule refresh without decoding the JWT. Never a client-generated value.

absolute_session_expires_at.description: Registry-authoritative absolute session deadline (#460 SEC-4A): after it, re-login is mandatory — refresh cannot extend it. The Web refresh cookie carries the same bound as its expiry.

endpoints.purpose: Onboarding Web por token de invitación

200.description: Invitation accepted and organization-scoped session created

Set-Cookie.description: Web onboarding is cookie-based today (#460 SEC-4A): the first refresh credential is set as the HttpOnly granete_web_refresh cookie and never appears in the body. A future mobile acceptance flow must extend this contract with an explicit transport first.

session_id.description: Server-side session registry id (#460). Present on tokens of version 5+; absent while a pre-#460 token is exchanged. Becomes required when the #460 SEC-9 gate retires version 4.

refresh_token.description: Opaque single-use refresh credential. Mobile-only transport (#460 SEC-4A): the mobile client stores it in its secure-store flow. Web never receives a refresh secret in JSON — its rotating credential is delivered exclusively as the HttpOnly granete_web_refresh Set-Cookie.

refresh_expires_at.description: Never later than the auth session absolute expiry. Mobile transport only.

access_expires_at.description: Server-clock instant the returned access token expires (#460 SEC-4A). Mirrors the minting arithmetic exactly so clients can schedule refresh without decoding the JWT. Never a client-generated value.

absolute_session_expires_at.description: Registry-authoritative absolute session deadline (#460 SEC-4A): after it, re-login is mandatory — refresh cannot extend it. The Web refresh cookie carries the same bound as its expiry.

findings.title: Legacy technical workflow lacks command capability and owner checks
findings.impact: Authenticated non-extension member in owning tenant can reach the legacy workflow mutation without handler-level role/owner restriction; force release bypasses loading check without mandatory reason. This is legacy technical_status, not normalized DesignRelease. No cross-tenant exploit demonstrated.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit command capability and project access checks; require authorized override with nonempty reason and durable atomic audit; minimize/redact response by capability.
findings.missingProof: Defensive routed denied-role/owner/override/audit rollback tests; runtime not executed. Full-project response has no handler redactor, but specific cost disclosure not independently proved.
